text: Acataphasia (or Akat- ) [Gr. a + kata + fanai , to speak]: Ger. Akataphasie ; Fr. paraphasie (see APHRASIA - P.J.); Ital. acatafusia . A disorder of speech appearing as an inability to connect words properly in sentences; a disorder of the syntactical arrangement of words. It is thus an aphasic defect which involves the most complicated components of spoken language. The coarse outlines of speech -- words and their meanings -- are understood and spoken, but their finer relations in the sentence are confused. The term was suggested by Steinthal and adopted by Kussmaul, Störungen der Sprache , chap. XXX. See SPEECH AND ITS DEFECTS. ( J.J. )
